title: Start June With a Simple Starting Rule
teaser: A repeatable way to begin can reduce friction before important work.
full_text: Choose one rule you will use when starting important work in June. Keep it small, such as spending the first ten minutes only on setup and the next visible action.

title: Turn an Expectation Into Observable Criteria
teaser: Vague expectations invite different definitions of success.
full_text: Replace one phrase like 'make it good' with two observable acceptance criteria today. Share them before the work is delivered.

title: Compare Two Learning Sources
teaser: A single source can be accurate and still leave important assumptions unstated.
full_text: Open a second reliable source on something you are learning. Pay special attention to definitions or assumptions that differ rather than only noting agreement.

title: Separate Fixed and Variable Cost
teaser: The same total expense can contain parts that respond to behavior and parts that do not.
full_text: Take one recurring expense and split it into fixed and usage-dependent portions. Focus improvement effort only on the part you can realistically influence.

title: Find the Shared Ground First
teaser: A disagreement is easier to discuss when the area of agreement is explicit.
full_text: In one difficult conversation today, state the point both sides already accept. Then move to the smaller issue where the real difference remains.

title: Give One Process a Single Owner
teaser: Many people can contribute to a workflow, but outcome ownership should not disappear.
full_text: Choose one recurring process and name the person responsible for tracking the final result. Keep contributors and outcome ownership as separate roles.

title: Map Energy Across the Week
teaser: Calendar hours look equal even when attention capacity is not.
full_text: Review the coming week and place demanding work in periods when your focus is usually stronger. Reserve lower-energy periods for simpler or more mechanical tasks.

title: Say One Small Need Clearly
teaser: Small unmet needs can become larger frustrations when they stay unspoken.
full_text: Tell someone you trust one small, real need today. Make it clear enough that they do not have to guess what would help.

title: Give a Document a Recheck Date
teaser: Some information remains correct only for a limited period.
full_text: Add a 'reverify after' date to one document that can become stale. Make the need for future validation visible to the next reader.

title: Assign Ownership to a Risk
teaser: A risk that belongs to everyone can end up being monitored by no one.
full_text: For one important risk, define who watches it, how often it is checked, and the first action if the warning sign appears.

title: Test a Rule With a Counterexample
teaser: Looking only at cases where a rule works can hide its real boundaries.
full_text: Create one example and one counterexample for a concept you are learning. Write the condition that separates when the rule applies from when it does not.

title: Make a Habit Visible With Minimal Tracking
teaser: A tiny record can support consistency without turning the habit into a data project.
full_text: Choose the simplest useful way to mark one habit today. If done/not done is enough, resist collecting extra detail you will not use.

title: Name the Worst Reasonable Outcome
teaser: Considering downside does not require imagining catastrophe.
full_text: For one important decision, write the worst outcome that is still realistically plausible. Decide what part you could tolerate and what part you can reduce before choosing.

title: Choose the Right Moment for Feedback
teaser: Useful feedback can lose value when delivered at a moment when the other person cannot process it.
full_text: Pick an appropriate time for one piece of feedback today. Unless safety is urgent, avoid forcing it into the middle of high pressure or distraction.

title: Freeze One Priority for the Rest of June
teaser: Constantly adding priorities can leave every important item half-finished.
full_text: Choose one priority that must be completed before you add another major commitment this month. Protect it until the finish line is visible.

title: Define When a Change Must Be Escalated
teaser: Not every small change needs an alert, but important drift should not stay hidden.
full_text: For one shared project, define the threshold that requires notifying others. Use time, budget, quality, or scope so the threshold is observable.

title: See the Opportunity Cost of a Purchase
teaser: Money committed to one option cannot serve another at the same time.
full_text: Before one planned purchase, write the most realistic alternative you are giving up. Evaluate the decision using both what you gain and what you forgo.

title: Group Errors Before Fixing Them
teaser: Treating every mistake as unique can hide a repeated pattern.
full_text: Sort several recent errors into simple categories such as process, information, attention, tool, or communication. Choose one prevention step for the most common category.

title: Set a Clear Response Window
teaser: Unclear timing can make a normal request feel more urgent than it is.
full_text: When sending an important request today, state when you actually need the response. If there is no hard deadline, give a reasonable window instead of creating false urgency.

title: Plan Recovery After a Busy Stretch
teaser: Capacity may not return instantly when an intense period ends.
full_text: Put a short recovery block after one demanding task or period today. Keep it available for decompression rather than automatically filling it with new work.

title: Read the Context Around the Claim
teaser: A sentence can be accurate and still become misleading when detached from its context.
full_text: For one important quote or claim, read the material immediately before and after it. Check whether the broader context changes the meaning you were using.

title: Define the Exception to a Boundary
teaser: A boundary can allow a real exception without dissolving into constant exceptions.
full_text: Write the one circumstance where you would genuinely make an exception to an important boundary. Keep the exception narrow enough that the rule still has meaning.

title: Choose the Observation Period Before the Experiment
teaser: Judging too early can turn normal variation into a false conclusion.
full_text: Before evaluating one small change, decide how long you will observe it. Avoid changing direction because of a single unusually good or bad day.

title: Remove One Meaningless Choice
teaser: Repeated low-value decisions create friction without improving the outcome.
full_text: In one recurring task, make one nonessential choice a default. Preserve judgment only where the choice actually changes quality or risk.

title: Return to Raw Examples When Quality Moves
teaser: Averages can hide whether the same problem is repeating or several different problems are mixed together.
full_text: If a quality metric changed, inspect at least three real examples before deciding on the cause. Let the examples shape the diagnosis.

title: Limit Inputs During a Focus Block
teaser: Too many open sources can turn focused work into endless research.
full_text: Set a limit on the number of tabs, documents, or references you will use in one focus session today. Work with what you have before opening another source.

title: Observe an Emotion Before Acting on It
teaser: The first intensity of an emotion may not match how it feels several minutes later.
full_text: When a strong emotion appears today, give it a short observation period before making an important decision. Notice intensity, trigger, and underlying need as separate pieces of information.

title: Identify the Nonnegotiable Part of the Plan
teaser: When conditions change, trying to preserve every detail can create unnecessary strain.
full_text: Choose the single outcome in one plan that truly must survive. Allow lower-priority details to change if that protects the essential result.

title: Rank Causes Before Choosing a Solution
teaser: The first explanation that comes to mind may be the most visible, not the most supported.
full_text: List at least three possible causes for one problem and rank them by evidence. Start intervention with the cause that has the strongest support.

title: Close June With One Deliberate Ending
teaser: A monthly review should identify what will stop as clearly as what will continue.
full_text: Choose one task, habit, or burden from June that you will not carry into July. Close it intentionally and leave a short note explaining why.
